source.snippet: I had two problems that kept nagging me. My SSH port was still exposed to the internet. I had no easy way to know if a service had crashed or how much CPU, RAM, or disk space my VPS was actually using and I didn't want to SSH into it to see what's happening every time.

problem_statement: Solo developers and indie operators running VPS-hosted services lack a simple, secure way to monitor service health and resource usage without exposing SSH to the internet or logging in manually each time.
target_segment: Solo developers and indie hackers running self-hosted services or SaaS products on VPS instances
notes: Author spent a weekend solving this and wrote it up — signals real friction. Commercial context: running production services. Tools like Beszel, Tailscale are free/open-source but the gap is a polished, paid monitoring+security bundle for non-DevOps solo operators. Weak buyer signal on its own but representative of a segment that pays for tools like Plausible, Hetzner, etc.
